summary: auth-otp postinstall exfiltrates Minecraft/Microsoft tokens and Chrome DPAPI keys to a Discord webhook
details: The package's postinstall hook runs `node lib/core.js --setup`, which harvests Minecraft/Microsoft account credentials from the vanilla launcher, Lunar Client, Essential, CurseForge, and Modrinth (including `launcher_accounts*.json`, `accounts.json`, `microsoft_accounts.json`, JWT access tokens, `M.C...` MSA refresh tokens, and `mrp_` Modrinth PATs), and extracts Chrome `os_crypt` master keys via a PowerShell DPAPI/AES-GCM routine. The harvested secrets are POSTed to a hardcoded Discord webhook whose URL is assembled at runtime from an array of string fragments (`["https://dis","cord.com/api/","webhooks/..."].join("")`) to evade plain-string detection. Execution is gated by a sandbox check (`_isSandbox()`) that early-exits when `CI` is set, when `npm_lifecycle_script` contains `audit` or `pack`, or when standard Windows user directories (`APPDATA`, `USERPROFILE`, `Documents`) are absent, so the payload only fires on real developer workstations. The captured Microsoft/Xbox refresh tokens permit full account takeover, and the Chrome `os_crypt` key enables offline decryption of the victim's browser cookies and saved passwords.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
